extra.message: User-supplied 'username' parameter is directly interpolated into a SQL query string via f-string on line 72. When vuln=1 (default), an attacker can inject arbitrary SQL through the username path parameter, e.g., passing "admin' OR '1'='1" to bypass authentication or extract data.

During user registration (line 60-66), if the 'admin' field is present in the request JSON and vuln=1, the client can directly set their own admin privileges. There is no server-side authorization check preventing a regular user from self-elevating to admin.

The debug endpoint (GET /users/v1/_debug) returns all users including plaintext passwords and admin flags. It has no authentication or authorization guard, exposing credentials to any unauthenticated caller.

The login endpoint (lines 101-106) returns distinct error messages for 'wrong password' versus 'username does not exist'. This enables username enumeration - an attacker can brute-force valid usernames by observing different responses.

cwe: CWE-198: Information Exposure Through Timing Behaviors

extra.message: When vuln=1 (default), the get_by_title endpoint (lines 50-51) returns a book's secret_content without verifying that the requesting user is the owner. Any authenticated user can retrieve another user's secret data by specifying any book_title.

The update_password endpoint (lines 186-192) when vuln=1 updates the password of any user identified by the path parameter 'username' rather than verifying it belongs to the authenticated session. Any authenticated user can change another user's password by crafting a request with a different username in the URL.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The OpenAPI spec exposes a /users/v1/_debug endpoint (lines 88-119) that is visible in the API documentation. This debug endpoint has no security scheme defined (unlike /me, /books/v1 POST, etc.), making it implicitly accessible to all users without any authentication requirement.

cwe: CWE-16: Configuration and Admin Management Errors

extra.message: The JWT secret key is hardcoded as the trivial string 'random' in config.py line 13. This makes it trivial for an attacker to forge valid authentication tokens since the signing key is publicly known.
Flask debug mode is enabled via debug=True in production app.py startup (line 17). This allows attackers to execute arbitrary Python code through the interactive debugger.

cwe: CWE-215: Information Exposure Through an Error Message

extra.message: The update_email endpoint (lines 144-145) uses a complex regex pattern with nested groups and backtracking that is vulnerable to ReDoS. An attacker can craft a malicious email string causing catastrophic backtracking, leading to denial of service.

JWT token decoding on line 48 does not validate the 'aud' (audience) claim. This could allow tokens issued for a different service to be accepted as valid if the same secret key is used across multiple services.

User passwords are stored in plaintext (line 15 defines password column, lines 85-89 set it during registration without any hashing). If the database is compromised, all user credentials are immediately exposed.

cwe: CWE-256: Plaintext Storage of a Password

extra.message: Line 73 uses SQLAlchemy text() with a dynamically constructed SQL string that includes user-supplied input. The text() construct in this context allows the entire query to be controlled by the attacker, enabling not just SQL injection but complete database manipulation.

The /createdb endpoint (lines 16-25) in the OpenAPI spec has no security scheme defined. This means any unauthenticated caller can wipe and repopulate the database with default credentials, effectively taking full control of the application.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The json_debug method (line 59) returns the plaintext password and admin flag alongside username and email. Any code path that calls this method will inadvertently leak credentials.

Token lifetime is set to a default of 60 seconds (line 12) via tokentimetolive environment variable. While this is short-lived, an attacker who intercepts a token only has 60 seconds. However combined with the hardcoded secret key, even a very short-lived token is attackable.
The application binds to 0.0.0.0 (line 17), making it accessible on all network interfaces. Combined with debug=True and no WSGI server, this exposes the application directly to external networks.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in 'Secure' Field Without Value
